newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Tchibo keeps coffee price stable for now.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Tchibo keeps coffee price stable for now.

text.p: Germany's second largest coffee roaster Tchibo Frisch-Roest-Kaffee GmbH is closely watching futures prices, but retail price rises are not planned for now, a spokeswoman said on Friday.
"We raised our prices on May 2 and will closely monitor the market over the next days and weeks, but there are no immediate plans to announce further increases," she said in response to an enquiry.
However, she added, "We assume further increases may become necessary at a later stage."
New York arabicas have staged dizzying rallies this week with contracts hitting 20-year highs on speculative buying against the background of tight supply.
For German roasters largely dependent on arabicas, with Tchibo a prime example, the buying-in price of some qualities has more than doubled since the start of the year.
Dollar firmness and high differentials added to raw materials costs, the spokeswoman said.
Tchibo, which last held a 19 percent share in the German roasted coffee market, raised its retail prices by 0.50-1.00 marks per 500 grams two weeks ago.
Its products are now offered at 8.99-10.99 marks, roughly one mark above the retail price average.
Competitor Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS), the market leader accounting for 35.5 percent of sales, on Monday said it planned a third round of price increases in 1997 for early June.
Ex-plant prices then would go up another 1.50-2.00 marks.
